cues: Good morning, HollowVale Harbor! You're listening to Sunny Side Up, on WKRS. I'm Marge.
And I'm Henry! And what a beautiful morning it is out there.
It certainly is, Henry. The gulls are up, the coffee's on, and the harbor is as calm as a bathtub.
We've got a full show for you today. Gardening, pet corner, a recipe, your letters, and of course, the dare of the day.
Let's start in the garden. Henry, how are your tomatoes this year?
Marge, I'm sorry to report that the tomatoes and I are no longer speaking.
The squirrels got to them first. I found one tomato with a single bite out of it, set right back on the vine. Very polite squirrels.
Well, my hydrangeas are doing wonderfully. And here's a little trick for everyone at home.
If you want your hydrangeas to turn purple or blue, tuck a few rusty nails into the soil around the roots.
Rusty nails! Is that really true?
Absolutely true. The flowers change color with the soil. Pink in sweet soil, blue and purple when it's a little sour.
I learn something new every single morning on this show.
And now, it's time for pet corner!
Our first letter comes from Mrs. Edna Pruitt, on Lantern Street. She writes: Dear Marge and Henry, my tabby cat, Pickles, has learned to open the bread box.
She continues. Every morning I find the bread box open and one slice of bread missing. Pickles doesn't eat it. She carries it out to the front porch and leaves it there.
Well, maybe she's feeding the birds. That's very generous of her.
A generous cat. Edna, we think Pickles is a treasure.
Next, a letter from young Tommy Hale, age nine, who wants to know if dogs can tell time.
Tommy, my old dog Biscuit used to sit by the door every evening at exactly half past five, waiting for me to come home. So I'd say yes, Tommy. Dogs know.
That's lovely, Henry. Now, I promised our listeners a recipe.
You did, and I've been looking forward to it all week.
Today it's my grandmother's clam chowder. You'll need two dozen clams, three potatoes, an onion, a little salt pork, a pint of milk, and a good pat of butter.
Cook the salt pork low and slow. Add the onion until it's soft, then the potatoes and the clam juice, and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Then in go the clams and the milk. And never let it boil once the milk is in.
Never let it boil. Write that down, everyone.
Serve it with oyster crackers and good company.
Now, a few notes from the community board.
The bake sale at the church hall is this Saturday. Mrs. Abernathy is bringing her famous blueberry pie, so come early.
The harbor master asks everyone to tie up at the north pier next week, while the main dock gets a fresh coat of paint.
And the library has new books in, including, Henry, a whole shelf on bird watching.
And now, the moment you've all been waiting for. The dare of the day!
Today's dare: tell somebody you love them before lunch.
It doesn't have to be fancy. A neighbor, a sister, a friend. Even the mailman.
Especially the mailman. He works very hard.
And a little bonus for our friends who are learning Ye Hukan. Today's word is son. It means happy.
Son! I'm very son this morning, Marge.
Kettle's on, door's open, and the coffee is always hot.
And we'll see you tomorrow morning, right here on WKRS.
